title: The ceiling refusal tells an operator in an IDE integrated terminal, where CLAUDECODE is also set, how to answer
goal: the refusal backlog.py answer and kbdecide.py print for a ceiling-class answer, and backlog.md and tools.md, name the IDE integrated-terminal case (CLAUDECODE is set there too, DOC S-exebozns) and the route the operator takes then (a standalone terminal), or the guard keys on CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, which IDE terminals do not set; which of the two is a gate for the operator

run: import sys;t=open('kb/_self/backlog.md',encoding='utf-8').read()+open('kb/_self/tools.md',encoding='utf-8').read();sys.exit(0 if 'integrated terminal' in t else 1)

gates.question: How does the ceiling guard treat an operator answering from an IDE integrated terminal, where CLAUDECODE is also set?
options: keep keying on CLAUDECODE; the refusal and the docs name the IDE case and send the operator to a standalone terminal
key on CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, which IDE terminals do not set
read both: refuse when either is set, and name the IDE route in the refusal
gates.recommendation: read both: refuse when either is set, and name the IDE route in the refusal

notes: Merged from ST-26viyxlk “The ceiling guard also reads CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION, and the docs call it a guard against carelessness, not a boundary” at the 2026-10-12 draft triage: in_agent_session still reads CLAUDECODE only (CHILD_SESSION returns False); it is the same signal-choice design as ST-4vaqzqyr (key on CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION or add it beside CLAUDECODE), and the two options conflict, so one story decides it; hardening only, no failure seen. Its goal: bl_authority.in_agent_session reads CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION (set in every subprocess Claude Code starts) besides CLAUDECODE, so a session command that clears CLAUDECODE alone ('CLAUDECODE= python3 _tools/backlog.py answer ...' or 'env -u CLAUDECODE ...') is still refused for a ceiling-class gate and a tests-ceiling decision; backlog.md and tools.md say the environment check guards against a careless delegated session, not one set on defeating it; any deny rule in .claude/settings.json for commands that clear these variables is the operator's call, asked as a gate Its checks: {"run": ["python3", "-c", "import sys;sys.path.insert(0,'_tools');import bl_authority as a;sys.exit(0 if a.in_agent_session({'CLAUDE_CODE_CHILD_SESSION':'1'}) else 1)"]} Its touches: _tools/bl_authority.py, _tools/test_authority.py, kb/_self/backlog.md, kb/_self/tools.md In SP-3trnelzv: the operator's Windows deploy runs in a VS Code workspace, so the busy-profile setting of ST-tac4z3zk (operator-only, outside an agent session) meets this case first.
